text.p: *Australian bond futures contracts ended the pre-weekend after hours session firm, but once again the 92.210/92.230 resistance area put a cap on the 10-year bond's advance.
*U.S. Treasuries firmed on a balanced budget accord.
*April ANZ jobs ads series at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond futures ended the pre-weekend after hours session firm but again the 92.210/92.230 resistance area put a cap on the 10-year contract's advance.
The contract ended SYCOM at 92.165 compared with Friday's pit close of 92.120 after briefly touching a high of 92.220.
The failure to breach this area yet again is expected to weigh heavily on the market and could see it drift back to first support 92.100.
A break here could see a further retracement to 92.030 and an eventual test of last week's 91.990 low, analysts said.

The firm undertone was in response to further strength in U.S. Treasuries after a balanced budget accord was finally reached in Washington on Friday. There was a mixed reaction to the key U.S. labour force report which saw non-farm payroll rise a smaller than expected 142,000, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.9 percent, its lowest level in 23 years.

However, there is a growing feeling among U.S. analysts that the Federal Reserve may hold fire in tightening policy when the Federel Open Market Committee meets on May 20 based on the recent data flow.
The Reserve Bank holds its monthly board meeting on Tuesday, although no policy change is expected to follow it after last week's stronger than expected first quarter average weekly earnings report.
The data killed off slim hopes of a further hopes monetary policy easing and economists generally expect the next move to up and possible occuring in the first quarter of next year.
However, further policy senstive data is due this week with Australia's own labour force report due on Thursday.
ANZ releases its April job advertisments series at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) today.
